references.text: Moses gave Gilead to Machir, as confirmed in this parallel account of the land distribution to the tribe of Manasseh.
Joshua describes how half of Gilead was given to Machir's descendants, confirming the allocation mentioned in Numbers.
Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh, received Gilead because he was a warrior—this elaborates on the background of the allocation.
Machir is mentioned as the son of Manasseh in the genealogy, and his descendants are called the Machirites.
Machir's children were born on Joseph's knees, showing Machir's significance in the lineage of Manasseh.
1 Chronicles confirms that Machir was the father of Gilead and describes the territory of his descendants.
Machir's lineage and his connection to Gilead are described in this genealogy.
